B09C001.summary: After Karna falls, Duryodhana appoints Shalya as commander, and Shalya is killed by Yudhishthira. Duryodhana hides in a lake and is found and killed by Bhima. Sanjaya returns to the Kuru capital and reports the ruin of the army to the blind king Dhritarashtra, who collapses. The chapter sets up the collapse of the Kaurava side and the grief that follows.

scenes.B09C001S01: Janamejaya asks what the surviving Kauravas did after Karna's fall. Vaishampayana tells how Shalya is killed, Duryodhana dies in the lake, and Sanjaya brings the news to Dhritarashtra, who faints and is comforted by Vidura.

shots.B09C001S01H01: Opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Sarasvati, before the narration begins.
shots.B09C001S01H02: Janamejaya asks what the remaining Kauravas did after Karna was killed, and how Duryodhana behaved toward the Pandavas.
shots.B09C001S01H03: Vaishampayana narrates Shalya's command and death, Duryodhana's flight into a lake and death at Bhima's hands, and Sanjaya's report to the king listing the dead.
shots.B09C001S01H04: Dhritarashtra faints on hearing the news, Vidura and the others revive him, and Vidura gently comforts him.

B09C002.summary: Dhritarashtra mourns his sons and laments that all the losses seem to be destiny. He recalls Duryodhana's boasts and the heroes who have now died. He turns to Sanjaya and asks for a full account of the battle, including who now leads the army and how the Pandavas and their allies fared.

scenes.B09C002S01: Dhritarashtra grieves for his sons, blames destiny for their deaths, and asks Sanjaya to describe the battle and the new commander's fate in detail.

shots.B09C002S01H01: Vaishampayana introduces Dhritarashtra's renewed lament after the women have been sent away.
shots.B09C002S01H02: Dhritarashtra mourns his sons, recalls their childhood, recounts Duryodhana's boasts about the allies he had, and concludes that all these losses must be destiny. He resolves to go into exile in the forest.
shots.B09C002S01H03: Vaishampayana says the king swoons again, then asks Sanjaya for the details of what happened.
shots.B09C002S01H04: Dhritarashtra asks who led the army after Drona and Karna fell, how Shalya and Duryodhana were killed, and asks Sanjaya to tell the whole account of the battle.

B09C003.summary: Sanjaya describes how the Kaurava army breaks and flees after Karna's death. Bhima and Dhrishtadyumna cut down the remaining troops, Arjuna scatters the rest, and Duryodhana alone tries to rally his men. He calls on them to fight to the end rather than run.

scenes.B09C003S01: Sanjaya tells how the Kaurava troops, leaderless after Karna's fall, are routed by the Pandavas and their allies, and how Duryodhana urges his men to stand and fight.

shots.B09C003S01H01: Sanjaya's full account of the rout: the panic after Karna's death, the Pandava attacks led by Bhima and Arjuna, and Duryodhana's speech urging his men to hold the field.

B09C004.summary: Kripa, seeing the army broken and the Pandavas' strength, urges Duryodhana to make peace. He reminds the king of the fallen heroes, of Arjuna's power and of the Pandavas' divine allies, and says the Kauravas cannot win. Kripa speaks in tears and nearly faints.

scenes.B09C004S01: Kripa, grieving over the battlefield, argues that the war is lost and advises Duryodhana to seek peace with Yudhishthira.

shots.B09C004S01H01: Sanjaya describes Kripa's appeal: he reminds Duryodhana of his dead allies, praises the Pandava warriors, and urges peace with Yudhishthira, then weeps and almost loses consciousness.

B09C005.summary: Duryodhana rejects Kripa's advice to make peace. He lists the wrongs the Pandavas have suffered at his hands and explains that he prefers death in battle to humiliation. He resolves to fight on, and the Kauravas camp for the night, ready to keep going.

scenes.B09C005S01: Duryodhana refuses peace, rehearses the grievances of the Pandavas and his own pride, and declares he will die fighting; the Kauravas camp near the field, resolved to continue the war.

shots.B09C005S01H01: Duryodhana thanks Kripa but says the advice does not suit him. He lists the reasons the Pandavas will never forgive him, including the dice game, Draupadi's humiliation and Abhimanyu's death.
shots.B09C005S01H02: Duryodhana says he will not give up his pride or his kingdom. He prefers a warrior's death, honours his fallen allies, and says the Kauravas' noble dead have gone to heaven. The Kshatriyas applaud, and the army camps by the Sarasvati river, resolved to fight on.

B09C006.summary: The Kaurava warriors camp at the foot of the Himalayas and need a new commander. Duryodhana asks Ashvatthama to choose one, and Ashvatthama names Shalya, who accepts. Duryodhana then formally asks Shalya to lead the army, and Shalya agrees to give his all.

scenes.B09C006S01: The Kauravas spend the night in the hills, Duryodhana asks Ashvatthama to name a commander, Ashvatthama proposes Shalya, and Shalya accepts the post.

shots.B09C006S01H01: Sanjaya describes the warriors camping in the hills, the Kaurava leaders' demand for a new commander, and Duryodhana approaching Ashvatthama, whom the text praises at length, to ask him to choose one.
shots.B09C006S01H02: Ashvatthama proposes Shalya as commander, citing his lineage, skill and loyalty, and the Kauravas cheer the choice.
shots.B09C006S01H03: Shalya accepts and promises to give everything he has to Duryodhana's service.
shots.B09C006S01H04: Duryodhana formally asks Shalya to take command and to fight as Kartikeya once did for the gods.

B09C007.summary: Shalya boasts that he alone can match the Pandava army and promises victory. He is formally installed as commander, and the Kauravas rejoice. In the Pandava camp, Yudhishthira worries about the new commander, and Krishna advises that Arjuna must kill Shalya, and the Pandavas sleep in relief.

scenes.B09C007S01: Shalya is installed as commander with rites and praise, boasts of his power, and the Pandavas respond when Krishna urges Arjuna to kill him.

shots.B09C007S01H01: Shalya tells Duryodhana he will lead the army and will beat the Pandavas, and Duryodhana formally installs him with water poured over him as the troops cheer.
shots.B09C007S01H02: Shalya vows to fight the Pandavas, Krishna and their allies that day, whether he wins or dies.
shots.B09C007S01H03: The Kauravas feel relieved and sleep well that night. Yudhishthira, hearing the news, asks Krishna what to do, and Krishna praises Shalya but urges Arjuna to kill him without pity. The Pandavas then rest, feeling victorious after Karna's fall.

B09C008.summary: The two armies arm and form up for a final battle, with the Kauravas under Shalya and the Pandavas under Yudhishthira. Dhritarashtra asks how Shalya and Duryodhana fell and asks for the strength of each army. Sanjaya gives the numbers and the dispositions of both sides, and the fighting begins at dawn.

scenes.B09C008S01: The Kauravas arm, pledge to fight together under Shalya, and the Pandavas form up to meet them, while Dhritarashtra asks how Shalya and Duryodhana were slain.
scenes.B09C008S02: Sanjaya describes Shalya's array and the Pandava divisions attacking different parts of the Kaurava force, and Dhritarashtra asks for the relative strength of the armies.
scenes.B09C008S03: Sanjaya gives the numbers of cars, elephants, horses and foot-soldiers on each side, and the battle begins at dawn.

shots.B09C008S01H01: Duryodhana orders his men to arm. The Kaurava warriors gear up, the Kaurava leaders swear to fight together, and the Pandavas advance, with the field looking like a swelling sea.
shots.B09C008S01H02: Dhritarashtra says he has heard of the fall of Drona, Bhishma and Karna, and asks what happened next.
shots.B09C008S01H03: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya to tell him of the fall of Shalya and his son.
shots.B09C008S01H04: Dhritarashtra asks how Yudhishthira slew Shalya.
shots.B09C008S01H05: Dhritarashtra asks how Bhima slew Duryodhana.
shots.B09C008S02H01: Sanjaya says he will describe the battle. He explains that the Kauravas hoped Shalya would destroy the Pandavas, and then describes Shalya's formation, the positions of the Kaurava commanders, and the Pandava divisions moving against them.
shots.B09C008S02H02: Dhritarashtra asks, after the fall of Bhishma, Drona and Karna, about the state of both sides.
shots.B09C008S02H03: Dhritarashtra's question continues, about the reduction of both armies.
shots.B09C008S02H04: Dhritarashtra's question continues, about the Pandavas' renewed anger in battle.
shots.B09C008S02H05: Dhritarashtra ends by asking Sanjaya about the strength of each army.
shots.B09C008S03H01: Dhritarashtra's question continues, asking for the strength of each army.
shots.B09C008S03H02: Sanjaya gives the numbers: about 11,000 cars, 10,700 elephants, 200,000 horses and three million foot-soldiers on the Kaurava side, and about 6,000 cars, 6,000 elephants, 10,000 horses and one million foot-soldiers left on the Pandava side. The two sides meet at dawn and the fighting becomes fierce.

B09C009.summary: Sanjaya describes the battle at its most violent, with bodies, elephants and chariots heaped on the field and the blood running like a river. Arjuna and Bhima stun the Kaurava army, and Dhrishtadyumna and Shikhandi attack Shalya. The Kaurava troops break and flee, leaving their leaders and kinsmen behind.

scenes.B09C009S01: Sanjaya describes the fierce, chaotic fighting between the Kurus and the Srinjayas, the heaps of dead, and the Kaurava rout after Bhima and Arjuna's attack.

shots.B09C009S01H01: Sanjaya describes the battle in grim detail: elephants, chariots and horsemen tear into one another, bodies and severed limbs cover the ground, and a river of blood carries the dead away. Bhima and Arjuna stun the Kaurava army, Dhrishtadyumna and Shikhandi turn on Shalya, and the Kaurava troops finally break and flee.

B09C010.summary: Shalya charges into the Pandava host and holds it back, and the Kauravas rally to him. Nakula kills Chitrasena and then Karna's sons Satyasena and Sushena in a long duel, with the help of Sutasoma. Shalya rallies the Kaurava troops, and the battle becomes a general slaughter on both sides.

scenes.B09C010S01: Shalya blocks the Pandava advance, Nakula defeats Karna's three sons one after another, and the armies clash in a general, bloody battle.

shots.B09C010S01H01: Sanjaya says Shalya drives straight at Yudhishthira and holds the Pandava army alone, so that the Kaurava troops return and a bloody battle breaks out.
shots.B09C010S01H02: Nakula duels Chitrasena and kills him, then fights Karna's sons Satyasena and Sushena, helped by Sutasoma. He kills Sushena and the Kaurava troops flee. Shalya rallies them, and the Pandava divisions turn on the Kaurava army and the battle becomes a general slaughter.

B09C011.summary: The battle grows more terrible as Shalya attacks the Pandava army and Yudhishthira. Omens appear, and the Kaurava commanders rush to protect Shalya. Bhima kills Shalya's driver with a mace after Shalya's lance hits him, and Shalya steps down from his chariot to face Bhima.

scenes.B09C011S01: Sanjaya describes the chaotic morning battle: Shalya attacks the Pandavas, omens appear, the Kaurava leaders protect Shalya, and Bhima fights Shalya with his mace.

shots.B09C011S01H01: Sanjaya describes the carnage in general terms: the troops slaughter one another, elephants cry out and cowards flee while the brave are glad.
shots.B09C011S01H02: The battle is fought at sunrise. The Pandava heroes, protected by Yudhishthira, fight the Kaurava army, which grows weak and frightened, like deer before a forest fire.
shots.B09C011S01H03: Shalya comes to rescue the weakened Kaurava army, and the Pandavas attack him with arrows while he keeps firing back at their host in Yudhishthira's sight.
shots.B09C011S01H04: Omens appear as the armies clash. Shalya pours arrows on Yudhishthira and the Pandava commanders, and the Kaurava leaders protect him. Bhima's horses are killed, Shalya kills Sahadeva's horses, and Sahadeva kills Shalya's son. Bhima fights on foot with his mace, smashes Kritavarma's car, and attacks Shalya, whose lance wounds Bhima. Bhima pulls it out and kills Shalya's driver, and Shalya steps down from his chariot. The Pandavas cheer Bhima.

B09C012.summary: Shalya and Bhima fight a long, even mace duel, and both fall after the force of their blows. Kripa carries Shalya off the field, but Bhima gets up and challenges him again. The battle then spreads across the field, with Duryodhana wounding Chekitana with a lance, and Shalya fighting Yudhishthira until Yudhishthira cuts down his standard and wounds him.

scenes.B09C012S01: Shalya and Bhima fight a mace duel to a stand-off, Kripa removes Shalya, and the general battle continues with Chekitana's death and a duel between Shalya and Yudhishthira.

shots.B09C012S01H01: Sanjaya describes the mace duel between Shalya and Bhima, the praise of the onlookers, the fall of both fighters, and Kripa carrying Shalya from the field. The fighting resumes with Duryodhana wounding Chekitana with a lance, Yudhishthira cutting down Shalya's standard, and Shalya, enraged, raining arrows on the Pandavas until Yudhishthira is worn down.

B09C013.summary: Satyaki, Bhima, Nakula, Sahadeva and Yudhishthira attack Shalya together, but he holds them off and destroys their weapons one by one. Yudhishthira worries that Shalya will destroy the Pandava army, and the Pandavas continue to press him. Shalya's arrows darken the sky, and even the gods are astonished by his skill.

scenes.B09C013S01: Five Pandava warriors attack Shalya at once, he blocks every attack, and Yudhishthira fears for his army as Shalya's arrows fill the sky.

shots.B09C013S01H01: Sanjaya describes the five Pandava warriors attacking Shalya together, Shalya's counterattacks, his destruction of their weapons, and the Pandava army's fear. Yudhishthira worries about Shalya's power, and the gods and Gandharvas are amazed as Shalya's arrows cover the field and the Pandavas press on.

B09C014.summary: Arjuna fights Drona's son Ashvatthama and the Trigarta warriors, and his arrows scatter the Kaurava troops across the field. Arjuna cuts down Ashvatthama's mallet and mace, and Ashvatthama then kills the Pancala warrior Suratha. Arjuna fights on alone against a large Kaurava force, and the fight is fierce.

scenes.B09C014S01: Arjuna clashes with Ashvatthama, who first blocks him and then kills Suratha, and Arjuna fights on against the Kaurava forces at noon.

shots.B09C014S01H01: Sanjaya describes Arjuna's attack on the Trigartas and Ashvatthama's army, his destruction of many cars, and his duel with Ashvatthama, in which neither can gain the upper hand. Ashvatthama kills Suratha and takes his chariot, and the fight at noon becomes fierce, with Arjuna alone against many.

B09C015.summary: Duryodhana fights Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandi meets Kritavarma and Kripa, and Shalya takes on the Pandava leaders one after another. He breaks Nakula's bow, then Satyaki charges him, and Shalya holds the field against many heroes. The chapter shows Shalya's skill as the Pandavas' main opponent.

scenes.B09C015S01: Shalya breaks Nakula's bow and then turns back Yudhishthira, Bhima, Sahadeva and Satyaki in turn, and his duel with Satyaki leaves the Pandavas struggling.

shots.B09C015S01H01: Sanjaya describes the wide battle: Duryodhana fights Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandi meets Kritavarma and Kripa, and Nakula wounds Shalya. Shalya breaks Nakula's bow and cars, then Yudhishthira, Bhima, Satyaki and Sahadeva all attack him. Satyaki's duel with Shalya ends in a mass of arrows across the field.

B09C016.summary: The Kaurava troops push the Pandavas back, and Shalya alone fights the whole Pandava army. Yudhishthira, enraged, vows to kill Shalya, arranges his chariot with his brothers and Krishna, and challenges him. Duryodhana is wounded, Shalya's chariot is cut down, and Shalya is carried off by Ashvatthama, leaving the Kauravas in disarray.

scenes.B09C016S01: Shalya leads the Kaurava advance against the Pandavas, Yudhishthira vows to kill him, and their duel leaves Shalya's chariot broken so that Ashvatthama must carry him away.

shots.B09C016S01H01: Sanjaya describes Shalya's push against the Pandavas, Yudhishthira's rage and vow to kill Shalya, and his plan for his chariot and protectors. The Pandavas and Pancalas attack. Bhima and Duryodhana fight, Duryodhana cuts Bhima's bow and standard, Bhima wounds Duryodhana and kills his driver. Yudhishthira destroys Shalya's steeds, drivers and standard, and Ashvatthama carries Shalya off the field.

B09C017.summary: Shalya fights Yudhishthira in a long, even duel, and Yudhishthira's dart finally kills him. Shalya falls with his face toward Yudhishthira, and his young brother is then killed too. The Kaurava army breaks in terror, and the Pandavas celebrate. Satyaki and Kritavarma also fight a duel, and Kritavarma is carried off.

scenes.B09C017S01: Shalya and Yudhishthira duel fiercely until Yudhishthira's dart kills Shalya, after which Shalya's brother falls, Satyaki and Kritavarma fight, and the Kaurava army flees.

shots.B09C017S01H01: Sanjaya describes the duel between Shalya and Yudhishthira, with Bhima, Satyaki, the twins and the Panchalas coming to Yudhishthira's aid. Shalya's arrows cut down bows, drivers, horses and armour. Yudhishthira, steedless and driverless, takes up a dart and hurls it, calling out that Shalya is slain.
shots.B09C017S01H02: Shalya tries to catch the dart but it pierces him, and he falls dead facing Yudhishthira. Shalya's younger brother attacks Yudhishthira and is killed. The Kauravas flee. Satyaki strips Kritavarma of his chariot and horses, Ashvatthama carries him off, and Duryodhana stands alone against the Pandavas. The Pandavas blow their conches and celebrate.

B09C018.summary: After Shalya dies, his 1,700 Madraka chariot warriors charge into the Pandava host despite Duryodhana's orders to hold back. Shakuni points out that the Kauravas must support them, and the whole Kaurava army moves to help. The Pandavas, however, destroy the Madrakas, and the Kaurava army flees.

scenes.B09C018S01: The Madrakas attack after Shalya's death, Duryodhana and Shakuni argue about the rescue, and the Pandavas defeat the Madrakas and the Kauravas flee.

shots.B09C018S01H01: Sanjaya describes the Madraka warriors, numbering about 1,700 chariots, pressing into the Pandava host while Duryodhana, on an elephant, orders them to stop. Arjuna and the other Pandavas come to Yudhishthira's rescue, and the Madrakas are cut down.
shots.B09C018S01H02: Duryodhana tells Shakuni that the Madrakas ignored his orders and went in together.
shots.B09C018S01H03: Shakuni says that angry warriors do not obey, that the Kauravas must now stand together, and that all of them should go to save the Madrakas. The Kauravas move forward, but the Pandavas destroy the Madrakas, and the whole Kaurava army turns and flees.

B09C019.summary: With Shalya dead, most of the Kaurava army flees in panic, and the Pandavas and Panchalas pursue them. Duryodhana tries to rally his troops, telling them that running is pointless and that they should die fighting. Bhima crushes 21,000 Kaurava foot-soldiers with his mace, and the Kauravas turn to fight again.

scenes.B09C019S01: After Shalya's fall the Kaurava army breaks, Duryodhana urges his men to make a stand, and Bhima destroys the foot-soldiers who attack him.

shots.B09C019S01H01: Sanjaya describes the rout after Shalya's death, the Pandava celebrations, Duryodhana's order to his driver to fall back, and Duryodhana's speech urging his men to stand and die fighting. Bhima, on foot with his mace, kills the foot-soldiers who surround him, and the Kaurava kings rally to fight again.

B09C020.summary: Salwa, king of the Mlecchas, rides a huge elephant into the Pandava army and drives it back in panic. Dhrishtadyumna attacks the elephant, which kills his chariot driver and horses. Bhima, Shikhandi and Satyaki stop the elephant, Dhrishtadyumna kills it with a mace, and Satyaki beheads Salwa with an arrow.

scenes.B09C020S01: Salwa's elephant routs the Pandava army, Dhrishtadyumna attacks it and is nearly crushed, and Satyaki kills Salwa after the elephant is slain.

shots.B09C020S01H01: Sanjaya describes Salwa on his great elephant routing the Pandava forces, Dhrishtadyumna's attack and his chariot being crushed, the Pandava heroes killing the elephant with mace and arrows, and Satyaki beheading Salwa as he falls with the elephant.

B09C021.summary: After Salwa's death the Kaurava army breaks, but Kritavarma rallies it and battles Satyaki. Satyaki kills Kshemakirti, then disarms and strips Kritavarma of his chariot. Kripa carries Kritavarma away, and Duryodhana stands alone against the Pandavas, while the Kaurava army once again flees.

scenes.B09C021S01: Kritavarma rallies the Kaurava army and fights Satyaki, who defeats him, and Duryodhana holds the field alone as the army retreats.

shots.B09C021S01H01: Sanjaya describes the rally after Salwa's death, Kritavarma's duel with Satyaki, Kritavarma's defeat and retreat with Kripa's help, and Duryodhana alone holding back the Pandava forces as the Kaurava army flees.

B09C022.summary: Duryodhana fights almost alone against the Pandavas, wounding each of them, and the Kaurava warriors rally round him. The fighting spreads into many single combats: Ashvatthama and Bhima, Shakuni and Yudhishthira, Uluka and Nakula, and Kripa against the sons of Draupadi. Dust covers the field until the blood settles it, and the battle goes on at noon.

scenes.B09C022S01: Duryodhana holds the field alone until his men return, and the battle breaks into many single combats across the field at noon.

shots.B09C022S01H01: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana's arrows covering the Pandava army and his wounding of each of the Pandava leaders. The Kaurava warriors return to him, and a long series of single combats follows, including Ashvatthama and Bhima, Shakuni and Yudhishthira, Uluka and Nakula, Kritavarma and Satyaki, and Duryodhana and Dhrishtadyumna. Sanjaya ends by noting the dust and the blood that settles it, and the noon fighting.

B09C023.summary: The Kauravas rally, but the battle turns into a chaotic slaughter in which Shakuni, with the Gandhara horsemen, attacks the Pandava rear. Yudhishthira sends Sahadeva and Draupadi's sons against him, and a massive, bloody cavalry and infantry struggle follows. Both sides are left exhausted, and Shakuni retreats with a small remnant, though the Kauravas and Pandavas go on killing one another, with omens of ruin all around.

scenes.B09C023S01: The Kauravas rally, Shakuni attacks the Pandava rear, and the battle becomes a wide and terrible carnage, after which Shakuni retreats with a small force and the fighting continues in disorder.

shots.B09C023S01H01: Sanjaya describes the Kauravas rallying after their defeat. Yudhishthira kills Kritavarma's four horses and wounds Kripa, Ashvatthama carries Kritavarma away, and Duryodhana sends seven hundred cars against Yudhishthira, who is rescued by the Pandava heroes. Omens appear. Shakuni attacks the Pandava rear with Gandhara horsemen, and Yudhishthira sends Sahadeva and Draupadi's sons against him. When Shakuni's men are beaten, he retreats with a small remnant. The Pandava horsemen then withdraw, and Shakuni returns to attack Dhrishtadyumna's division, and the struggle goes on in disorder until the Pandavas encircle Shakuni and the combat ends in mutual slaughter.

B09C024.summary: Shakuni rallies his last seven hundred horsemen and sends them against the Pandavas, claiming the Pandava chariots are already beaten. Arjuna answers Krishna with a bitter speech, blaming Duryodhana's obstinacy for a war that should have ended after Bhishma's fall, and vowing to kill the Kaurava warriors. He then drives into the enemy host and burns through its ranks with his arrows.

scenes.B09C024S01: Shakuni urges the Kaurava warriors forward, Arjuna blames Duryodhana for the endless war and vows to kill everyone, and Arjuna drives into the enemy host with Krishna and destroys it with his arrows.

shots.B09C024S01H01: Sanjaya describes Shakuni gathering seven hundred horsemen and telling Duryodhana to attack. Arjuna, seeing the Kauravas come on, tells Krishna the war should have ended after Bhishma, Drona and Karna fell, blames Duryodhana's folly and Vidura's warnings, and vows to kill the Kaurava warriors that day.
shots.B09C024S01H02: Sanjaya describes Krishna driving Arjuna into the Kaurava host, Arjuna's arrows striking men, horses and elephants, and his single-handed destruction of the Kaurava divisions.

B09C025.summary: Arjuna's arrows scatter the Kaurava army, and many of its warriors flee or fall. Dhrishtadyumna kills Duryodhana's horses and driver, and Duryodhana rides off on horseback. Three thousand Kaurava elephants surround the Pandavas, but Arjuna and Bhima destroy them. Ashvatthama, Kripa and Kritavarma search for Duryodhana, and a Kuru warrior, captured by Satyaki, tells how the Kauravas were beaten.

scenes.B09C025S01: Arjuna scatters the Kaurava army, Duryodhana loses his chariot and flees, Bhima and Arjuna destroy the elephant force, and Ashvatthama and his companions go looking for Duryodhana.

shots.B09C025S01H01: Sanjaya describes the Kaurava army fleeing and regrouping, Dhrishtadyumna's attack on Duryodhana, the loss of Duryodhana's chariot, and the Kaurava elephants that surround the Pandavas. Arjuna and Bhima kill the elephants, and Ashvatthama, Kripa and Kritavarma search for Duryodhana. A Kuru warrior, speaking in the first person, recounts his defeat by Dhrishtadyumna and his capture by Satyaki.

B09C026.summary: After the elephant division is destroyed, Duryodhana's brothers charge Bhima together, and Bhima kills them one by one. Srutarvan, the last of them, attacks Bhima, is disarmed, and is beheaded. Bhima then cuts down hundreds of Kaurava chariots, elephants, foot-soldiers and horses, and the surviving Kaurava army is left very thin.

scenes.B09C026S01: Duryodhana's brothers rush Bhima, Bhima kills them one after another, and then he mows down the Kaurava army until very few are left.

shots.B09C026S01H01: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana's brothers, who unite against Bhima while Duryodhana is missing. Bhima kills them one by one. Srutarvan fights on, Bhima kills his driver and horses, and Srutarvan is beheaded after taking up a sword and shield. Bhima then slaughters hundreds of chariots, elephants, foot-soldiers and horses, and the Kaurava army is left very thin and cheerless.

B09C027.summary: Only Duryodhana and his son Sudarsana are left of Dhritarashtra's sons, and Duryodhana stays among his cavalry. Krishna urges Arjuna to strike at him, and Arjuna boasts that he will kill the remaining Kaurava warriors. Arjuna, Bhima and Sahadeva attack, Duryodhana wounds Sahadeva, and Arjuna destroys the Trigartas, while Bhima kills Sudarsana. The Kauravas are left in a desperate fight.

scenes.B09C027S01: Krishna and Arjuna plan the attack on Duryodhana, Arjuna cuts down the Trigarta leaders and the cavalry, and Bhima kills Sudarsana while the fighting spreads.

shots.B09C027S01H01: Sanjaya describes Krishna urging Arjuna to strike at Duryodhana, who stands among his cavalry, and Arjuna answering that he will kill Duryodhana and the other remnants. Arjuna, Bhima and Sahadeva charge, Duryodhana lances Sahadeva, Arjuna slays the Trigarta leaders and their followers, and Bhima kills Sudarsana. The battle turns into a bloody general fight in which both sides fall, wailing for their kin.

B09C028.summary: Shakuni attacks Sahadeva, while Bhima fights Uluka, and the battle becomes a field of severed limbs. Duryodhana urges the fleeing Kauravas back into the fight. Sahadeva kills Uluka and then breaks Shakuni's weapons one by one. He finally cuts off Shakuni's head, and the Kaurava army flees in terror.

scenes.B09C028S01: Sahadeva fights Shakuni and Uluka, Duryodhana rallies the troops, Sahadeva kills Uluka and then Shakuni, and the Kauravas flee while the Pandavas celebrate.

shots.B09C028S01H01: Sanjaya describes the dreadful carnage as the Kaurava army shrinks to a remnant, and Duryodhana urges his fleeing troops back into the fight. Sahadeva kills Uluka, then breaks Shakuni's bow and his scimitar, mace and dart. Chasing Shakuni, Sahadeva cuts off his umbrella, standard, bow, arms and finally his head. The Kauravas flee in fear, and the Pandavas celebrate and praise Sahadeva.

B09C029.summary: The last Kaurava troops are wiped out and Duryodhana, alone and wounded, flees to a lake and hides in it by magic. Sanjaya is spared by Vyasa's intervention, finds Duryodhana at the lake, and hears his lament. The surviving Kaurava warriors and women flee the camp, and Yuyutsu brings the news to Vidura in Hastinapura.

scenes.B09C029S01: Duryodhana's last army is destroyed and he hides in a lake, Sanjaya is released and reports to Duryodhana, and the camp and capital are thrown into panic and grief.

shots.B09C029S01H01: A heading: the Hrada-pravesa Parva, the section title.
shots.B09C029S01H02: Sanjaya describes the last Kaurava rally, the Pandava assault that destroys it, and Duryodhana, the only survivor, fleeing on foot in grief and fear.
shots.B09C029S01H03: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya how many Pandava troops remained and what Duryodhana did when his army was destroyed.
shots.B09C029S01H04: Sanjaya gives the Pandava remnant's numbers, tells how Duryodhana fled into a lake, and recounts how Satyaki was about to kill him until Vyasa stopped him. He describes meeting Duryodhana, who hides in the lake by illusion and sends a message to Dhritarashtra. Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma find Sanjaya, and the women and camp-followers flee the camp in panic. Yuyutsu reaches Hastinapura with them, and Vidura praises him and tells him to rest before returning to Yudhishthira.

B09C030.summary: Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma go to the lake and urge Duryodhana to fight on. Duryodhana, weary and wounded, refuses until the next day. Ashvatthama swears to kill every Panchala that night, but a group of huntsmen overhears the conversation and tells the Pandavas where Duryodhana is hiding. The Pandavas come to the lake, and the three warriors leave to rest under a banyan tree.

scenes.B09C030S01: Dhritarashtra asks what the surviving Kaurava warriors did, Sanjaya describes their visit to the hidden Duryodhana, the huntsmen's tip-off, the Pandava arrival at the lake, and the three warriors' departure.

shots.B09C030S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks what the surviving Kaurava warriors, Kritavarma, Kripa and Ashvatthama, did after the army was destroyed, and what Duryodhana did.
shots.B09C030S01H02: Sanjaya describes the three warriors going to the lake, the Pandavas searching the field for Duryodhana, and the warriors urging the king from under the water to rise and fight.
shots.B09C030S01H03: Duryodhana says he is too tired and wounded to fight now, asks his friends to rest, and promises to fight the next morning.
shots.B09C030S01H04: Ashvatthama swears to slay every Panchala that night and the warriors insist on battle. Meanwhile, huntsmen who supplied Bhima with meat overhear the talk, find the Pandavas and tell them where Duryodhana is hidden. The Pandavas, Krishna and the others ride to the lake, and Duryodhana, hidden in the water, hears them coming. Kripa, Kritavarma and Ashvatthama leave and rest under a banyan tree.

B09C031.summary: The Pandavas reach the lake where Duryodhana is hidden by his magic. Krishna urges Yudhishthira to fight illusion with cunning, citing past victories won by stratagem. Yudhishthira taunts Duryodhana for hiding like a coward. Duryodhana replies that he only rested from exhaustion, then declares he no longer wants the earth, which is empty of heroes, and offers to give it up and retire to the forest. Yudhishthira refuses the gift and insists that the Kauravas must fight.

scenes.B09C031S01: Yudhishthira and Krishna reach the enchanted lake, Krishna urges cunning, and Yudhishthira taunts Duryodhana, who answers from the water.
scenes.B09C031S02: Duryodhana says he hid only from exhaustion and then offers the earth to the Pandavas, but Yudhishthira refuses to accept a gift and reminds him of the past wrongs done to them.

shots.B09C031S01H01: Sanjaya describes the Pandavas arriving at the lake where Duryodhana is hiding by magic. Yudhishthira says Duryodhana has used illusion and that he will still be killed that day, even if Indra helps him.
shots.B09C031S01H02: Krishna tells Yudhishthira to answer illusion with his own cunning, and recalls many old victories won by stratagem, such as those of Indra, Vishnu and Rama.
shots.B09C031S01H03: Yudhishthira taunts Duryodhana: he calls him a boaster who hides in a lake instead of fighting, and tells him to rise and either win the earth or die fighting.
shots.B09C031S01H04: Sanjaya introduces Duryodhana's reply, which he gives from inside the water after hearing Yudhishthira's words.
shots.B09C031S01H05: The sentence continues: Duryodhana answers Yudhishthira from within the waters.
shots.B09C031S02H01: Duryodhana says he did not flee from fear but because his chariot, quivers and drivers were gone and he was alone, so he needed rest. He promises to rise and fight.
shots.B09C031S02H02: Yudhishthira says the Pandavas have rested and searched long enough, and tells Duryodhana to rise and fight, either to win the kingdom or to die a hero's death.
shots.B09C031S02H03: Duryodhana says his brothers and allies are dead, the earth is now like a widow, and he no longer wants it. He offers to give it to the Pandavas and retire to the forest in deerskin.
shots.B09C031S02H04: Yudhishthira refuses the gift, saying a Kshatriya cannot accept such a gift and that Duryodhana never gave them even a needle's point of land. He recalls the attempts to burn and poison the Pandavas and Draupadi's humiliation, and says Duryodhana must fight.
shots.B09C031S02H05: Sanjaya says the victorious Pandavas continue to rebuke and mock Duryodhana.

B09C032.summary: Duryodhana rises from the lake, armed with his mace, and taunts the Pandavas. He says he is alone and unfit to face so many, but he offers a one-on-one mace duel. Yudhishthira agrees and promises him the kingship if he kills one of them. Yudhishthira then rebukes him for the killing of Abhimanyu, and Duryodhana arms himself and challenges the brothers to fight him one by one.

scenes.B09C032S01: Dhritarashtra asks how Duryodhana answered the taunts, Duryodhana protests that he is alone and offers a fight, and Yudhishthira agrees to a one-on-one contest.
scenes.B09C032S02: Duryodhana chooses the mace, rises from the lake, and challenges the Pandavas to a one-on-one mace duel, and Yudhishthira urges him to fight.
scenes.B09C032S03: Yudhishthira rebukes Duryodhana for the killing of Abhimanyu and again offers the kingship to the winner, and Duryodhana arms himself and challenges the brothers to fight.

shots.B09C032S01H01: A heading: the Gada-yuddha Parva, the section title for the mace duel.
shots.B09C032S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks how his son, so proud and never before spoken to like this, could take such taunts, and asks Sanjaya to tell him exactly what was said.
shots.B09C032S01H03: Sanjaya says Duryodhana heard the taunts from within the water, grew miserable, sighed heavily, and answered the Pandavas from the lake.
shots.B09C032S01H04: Duryodhana says the Pandavas have their friends and chariots while he is alone and without a chariot, so he cannot fight them all at once. He asks them to fight him one at a time, and promises to rise and fight them all with his mace.
shots.B09C032S01H05: Yudhishthira praises Duryodhana's courage and agrees to a one-on-one fight with any weapon he chooses, promising him the kingship if he kills one of the brothers.
shots.B09C032S02H01: Duryodhana chooses the mace as his weapon and asks any one of the Pandavas to come forward and fight him on foot.
shots.B09C032S02H02: Yudhishthira tells Duryodhana to rise and fight them one at a time, to be a man, and that he will die that day even if Indra helps him.
shots.B09C032S02H03: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana rising from the lake with his iron mace, in angry, blazing splendour, and warning the Pandavas that he will kill them all.
shots.B09C032S02H04: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana standing on the bank, bloody and dripping, looking like the wrathful sun, as he summons the Pandavas to battle.
shots.B09C032S02H05: Duryodhana repeats that he will fight only one of them at a time, since fighting many at once would be improper for a man who is armourless and exhausted, and asks the gods to see the fight.
shots.B09C032S03H01: Yudhishthira rebukes Duryodhana for joining many warriors to kill Abhimanyu, says the Kshatriya code is cruel, and again offers the kingship to whichever brother he kills.
shots.B09C032S03H02: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana arming himself in golden mail and a golden helmet, and challenging Sahadeva, Bhima, Nakula, Arjuna or Yudhishthira to a mace fight, promising to beat whoever accepts.

B09C033.summary: Krishna criticises Yudhishthira for offering the kingship to whoever kills a Pandava, arguing that Duryodhana is too skilled with the mace. Bhima answers that he will fight Duryodhana and kill him, and he speaks of the Pandavas' many wrongs. Duryodhana replies with defiance, boasting that he has never been beaten in fair combat and that the Pandavas have suffered enough. The two heroes are set to fight with maces.

scenes.B09C033S01: Krishna questions Yudhishthira's rash offer, Bhima accepts the challenge and recounts the Kauravas' wrongs, and Duryodhana answers with boasts and defiance before the duel.

shots.B09C033S01H01: Krishna blames Yudhishthira's rash offer. He says Duryodhana has practised with the mace for thirteen years and, being so skilled, could beat any Pandava except Bhima. He calls the Pandavas' destiny one of exile.
shots.B09C033S01H02: Bhima tells Krishna not to grieve, promises to kill Duryodhana, and says his mace is heavier than Duryodhana's.
shots.B09C033S01H03: Krishna praises Bhima, lists the Kauravas killed in battle, and urges him to be careful. Bhima accepts the challenge, recalls the wrongs of Varanavata, the dice game and Draupadi's humiliation, and tells Duryodhana that he alone is left of his line.
shots.B09C033S01H04: Duryodhana answers that Bhima's words are empty and boasts that he has never lost a fair fight. He says he is the one who drove the Pandavas into the forest and into disguise. He warns that if the Pandavas beat him by trickery their shame will last. The Pandavas and Srinjayas cheer, and the weapons of the Pandavas begin to blaze.

B09C034.summary: Balarama arrives at the field to watch the mace duel between his two pupils, Bhima and Duryodhana. The Pandavas and Krishna greet him warmly, and he takes his seat among the kings to witness the contest.

scenes.B09C034S01: Balarama arrives at the battlefield, is greeted with honour by the Pandavas and Krishna, and takes his seat to watch the duel between Bhima and Duryodhana.

shots.B09C034S01H01: Sanjaya describes Balarama's arrival at the field as the two pupils prepare to fight, his greeting by the Pandavas and Krishna, his remarks about his journey, and his seat among the kings for the duel.

B09C035.summary: Janamejaya asks why Balarama left the war and where he went. Vaishampayana explains that Balarama, unwilling to take either side, toured the Sarasvati river and its sacred sites, giving gifts along the way until he reached Kurukshetra. He begins the list of sacred spots with Prabhasa, where the moon was cured of a wasting curse.

scenes.B09C035S01: Janamejaya asks about Balarama's absence, and Vaishampayana tells how Balarama left the war, made a pilgrimage along the Sarasvati with many gifts, and began to describe its sacred sites.
scenes.B09C035S02: Vaishampayana tells how Daksha cursed Soma with wasting for favouring Rohini, how the gods pleaded for him, and how Soma was restored by bathing at Prabhasa, which gave the place its name.

shots.B09C035S01H01: Janamejaya asks why Balarama left the war, and Vaishampayana is asked to tell where he went and how he saw the battle.
shots.B09C035S01H02: Vaishampayana explains that Krishna failed to reconcile the sides and that Balarama, angry at Krishna's refusal to help the Kurus, set out on a pilgrimage along the Sarasvati. He gave away large gifts to Brahmanas and the needy at many sacred sites, and finally reached Kurukshetra.
shots.B09C035S01H03: Janamejaya asks for the origin, features and merits of the sacred sites on the Sarasvati, and the rules for visiting them.
shots.B09C035S01H04: Vaishampayana begins with Prabhasa, where the moon was cured of his phthisis, and explains that the place is named for the restoration of Soma's splendour.
shots.B09C035S01H05: Janamejaya asks why Soma was cursed and how he was cured at the place.
shots.B09C035S02H01: Vaishampayana tells how Daksha's twenty-seven daughters, wives of Soma, complained that he favoured Rohini. Daksha ordered Soma to treat them equally, but he did not, so Daksha cursed him with wasting. The herbs and creatures declined, and the gods pleaded with Daksha to lift the curse. Daksha agreed that Soma would wax and wane but would be restored if he bathed at Prabhasa. Soma bathed there and was restored. Balarama then visited Chamasodbheda and Udapana, where the Sarasvati seems to disappear underground.

B09C036.summary: Balarama bathes at the sacred pool of Udapana, which Vaishampayana ties to the story of the ascetic Trita. Trita's two brothers left him to die in a well, but he performed a sacrifice in his mind, the Sarasvati rose to lift him out, and he cursed his brothers to become wolves. The chapter is part of Balarama's tour of the holy places along the Sarasvati.

scenes.B09C036S01: Balarama visits Udapana, Vaishampayana tells the story of Trita, the sage abandoned by his brothers and rescued by the Sarasvati, and Balarama moves on.

shots.B09C036S01H01: Vaishampayana says Balarama goes on to Udapana, where the ascetic Trita once lived, and gives gifts and bathes there. The chapter gives the background: Trita drank Soma in a pit, and his brothers threw him down and cursed.
shots.B09C036S01H02: Janamejaya asks how Udapana came about, why Trita fell into a pit, why his brothers abandoned him, and how he performed his sacrifice.
shots.B09C036S01H03: Vaishampayana tells the story: three brothers, Ekata, Dwita and Trita, sons of Gautama, travel with cattle after a sacrifice. The two elder brothers decide to steal the cattle and leave Trita. A wolf frightens Trita into a dry well, and he performs a sacrifice in his mind. The gods come for their shares, the Sarasvati rises to lift him out, and Trita curses his brothers to become wolves, leopards, bears and apes. Balarama then bathes at Udapana and goes on to Vinasana.

B09C037.summary: Balarama tours a series of sacred places along the Sarasvati, including Vinasana, Subhumika, the Gandharva shrine, Gargasrota, Sankha and Nagadhanwana. The river turns east so that the sages of Naimisha can find room for their rites, and Balarama reaches Sapta-Saraswat, where the sage Mankanaka once performed penances.

scenes.B09C037S01: Balarama visits a series of holy sites along the Sarasvati, gives gifts at each, and sees the river turn east to make room for the Naimisha sages, before he reaches Sapta-Saraswat.

shots.B09C037S01H01: Vaishampayana describes Balarama's visits to Vinasana, Subhumika, the Gandharva tirtha, Gargasrota, Sankha, the Dwaita lake and Nagadhanwana, and the gifts he gives at each. Past Nagadhanwana, he reaches the point where the Sarasvati turns east, and he is amazed.
shots.B09C037S01H02: Janamejaya asks why the Sarasvati bends eastward and why Balarama was astonished by it.
shots.B09C037S01H03: Vaishampayana explains that the Naimisha sages, after a twelve-year sacrifice, crowded the banks of the Sarasvati and had nowhere to hold their rites. The river made room for them by changing course, then returned westward. Balarama, wondering at this, visits Sapta-Saraswat, where the sage Mankanaka had performed penances.

B09C038.summary: Janamejaya asks why the place is called Sapta-Saraswat and who Mankanaka was. Vaishampayana explains that the Sarasvati appears in seven forms, which join at this place, and recounts several sacrifices where she manifested. He then tells how Mankanaka's seed, kept in a jar, became seven sages, and how Mankanaka danced in delight at a juice that flowed from his wound until Mahadeva showed him ash and taught him humility.

scenes.B09C038S01: Vaishampayana names the seven forms of the Sarasvati, tells of her appearances at sacrifices, and then narrates Mankanaka's story, including his dance and his lesson from Mahadeva.

shots.B09C038S01H01: Janamejaya asks why the tirtha is called Sapta-Saraswat, who Mankanaka was, and how he became successful, asking about his vows and learning.
shots.B09C038S01H02: Vaishampayana names the seven forms of the Sarasvati and tells how she appeared at sacrifices held by Brahma at Pushkara, by the sages at Naimisha, by Gaya, Auddalaka, Kuru, Daksha and Brahma, and how the seven joined at Sapta-Saraswat. He then tells how Mankanaka, a young ascetic, saw a woman bathing, and his seed fell into the river and was kept in a jar, where it became seven sages, fathers of the Maruts. Later a Kusha blade cut his hand, a juice flowed out, and he danced with joy until the gods went to Mahadeva.
shots.B09C038S01H03: Mahadeva asks why Mankanaka is dancing. The sage answers that he sees a juice from his wound, and Mahadeva shows him ash from his own thumb. Mankanaka recognises Rudra, praises him, and asks forgiveness. Mahadeva promises that anyone who worships at Sapta-Saraswat will reach the realm of the Sarasvati after death, and the chapter ends by noting that Mankanaka was a son of the wind god by Sukanya.

B09C039.summary: Balarama goes on to Usanas, also called Kapalamochana, where Sukra once performed penance. Janamejaya asks how the place got its name, and Vaishampayana tells how Rama's severed Rakshasa head stuck to the thigh of the sage Mahodara until he bathed at the tirtha and was freed. Balarama then visits the asylum of Rushangu and nearby holy places.

scenes.B09C039S01: Balarama visits Usanas and Kapalamochana, Janamejaya asks about it, Vaishampayana tells the story of Mahodara's release, and Balarama moves on to Rushangu's asylum and other holy places.

shots.B09C039S01H01: Vaishampayana says Balarama worships the dwellers of the tirtha and goes on to Usanas, also called Kapalamochana, where Sukra performed penances and where Rama once threw a Rakshasa's head.
shots.B09C039S01H02: Janamejaya asks why the place is called Kapalamochana and how the head came to stick to the sage.
shots.B09C039S01H03: Vaishampayana tells how Rama killed a Rakshasa in Dandaka and his severed head fell on the thigh of Mahodara, who was wandering. The head stuck to him, and he went all over the holy places in pain until he heard of this sacred spot and bathed in it. The head fell into the water and was lost, and the sage was freed. Balarama then gives gifts and goes on to Rushangu's asylum, where Arshtishena performed penance, and to other holy places like it.

B09C040.summary: Janamejaya asks how Arshtishena, Sindhudwipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra gained the status of Brahmanas. Vaishampayana tells how Arshtishena, after failing to learn in his teacher's house, won mastery of the Vedas through penance and gave the place its boons. He then tells how the Kshatriya king Vishvamitra, defeated by Vasishtha's magic cow, did austerities at this tirtha and became a Brahmana.

scenes.B09C040S01: Janamejaya asks about the Brahmana-hood of several sages, and Vaishampayana describes Arshtishena's penance and boons and Vishvamitra's rise from king to Brahmana.

shots.B09C040S01H01: Janamejaya asks how Arshtishena, Sindhudwipa, Devapi and Vishvamitra gained the status of Brahmanas, and asks for full details.
shots.B09C040S01H02: Vaishampayana tells how Arshtishena failed to master his lessons, did penance, won mastery of the Vedas, and gave the place three boons. He then tells how Vishvamitra, a king, left his throne to his son Vishvamitra, lost control of his kingdom, and attacked Vasishtha's hermitage. Vasishtha's cow created warriors who routed his army. Vishvamitra then did penance at this tirtha, won the boon of Brahmanhood from Brahma, and wandered the earth as a Brahmana. Balarama then gave gifts there and went on to Vaka's asylum.

B09C041.summary: Balarama reaches the asylum of the sage Dalvya Vaka, who once cursed King Dhritarashtra's kingdom through a sacrifice after the king mocked him over dead cattle. The king begged forgiveness and the kingdom was restored. Vaishampayana then tells of Brihaspati and Yayati's sacrifices at this river site, before Balarama moves on to Vasishthapavaha.

scenes.B09C041S01: Balarama visits Vaka's asylum, Vaishampayana tells how Vaka's curse on Dhritarashtra's kingdom was lifted, and then tells of other sacrifices there before Balarama moves on.

shots.B09C041S01H01: Vaishampayana describes Balarama at Vaka's asylum, the sage Dalvya Vaka's sacrifice that poured Dhritarashtra's kingdom into the fire, and how the kingdom wasted away. Counsellors blamed the king's insult over the dead cattle, and the king begged Vaka's forgiveness at the riverbank, after which the kingdom was freed and Vaka returned to Naimisha.
shots.B09C041S01H02: Vaishampayana tells how Brihaspati made a sacrifice here with flesh to destroy the Asuras, and how Yayati's sacrifice at the Sarasvati produced milk and butter and gifts for the guests. Balarama then gives generous gifts and moves on to the sacred river site called Vasishthapavaha.

B09C042.summary: Janamejaya asks why the Vasishthapavaha current is so swift and what caused the feud between Vasishtha and Vishvamitra. Vaishampayana tells how the rival sages fought for superiority, how Vishvamitra ordered the Sarasvati to bring Vasishtha so that he could kill him, and how the river carried Vasishtha to Vishvamitra's bank and back. Angered by the trick, Vishvamitra cursed the river to flow with blood for a year.

scenes.B09C042S01: Janamejaya asks about the feud, and Vaishampayana describes the rivalry, the Sarasvati's flight with Vasishtha, and Vishvamitra's curse on the river.

shots.B09C042S01H01: Janamejaya asks why the Vasishthapavaha current is so rapid, why the river carried off Vasishtha, and what caused the quarrel between Vasishtha and Vishvamitra.
shots.B09C042S01H02: Vaishampayana describes the rivalry of the two sages on opposite banks, the holy site called Sthanu-tirtha, and Vishvamitra's plan. He orders the Sarasvati to bring Vasishtha to him so that he can kill him, and the frightened river goes to Vasishtha to tell him.
shots.B09C042S01H03: Vasishtha tells the river to save herself. She washes away one bank and carries him to Vishvamitra's side, where he praises her. Vishvamitra, enraged, curses the Sarasvati to flow with blood. She flows that way for a year, and the place is named Vasishthapravaha. Later the river recovers its proper course.

B09C043.summary: The cursed Sarasvati flows with blood, and Rakshasas gather to drink it. Sages purify the river, and the Rakshasas are freed by rules about the foods they may eat, and the river is turned into the Aruna branch. Indra, guilty of killing his friend Namuchi, is cleansed by bathing at this confluence. Balarama then visits the Soma tirtha, where Skanda won his command after defeating Taraka.

scenes.B09C043S01: The sages purify the Sarasvati, the Rakshasas are freed, and Indra bathes at the Aruna confluence to be cleansed of killing Namuchi.
scenes.B09C043S02: Balarama bathes at the Soma tirtha, a site linked to Skanda's victory over Taraka and his command of the gods' army.

shots.B09C043S01H01: Vaishampayana describes the Sarasvati flowing with blood, the Rakshasas drinking it and dancing, and the sages' decision to purify her. The Rakshasas beg for relief, and the sages teach them which foods are forbidden. The river takes the new form of Aruna, the Rakshasas are freed, and Indra bathes there to be cleansed of his sin.
shots.B09C043S01H03: Janamejaya asks why Indra was tainted by the sin of killing a Brahmana.
shots.B09C043S01H04: Janamejaya continues, asking how Indra was cleansed by bathing at the tirtha.
shots.B09C043S01H05: Vaishampayana tells how Indra made a covenant with Namuchi not to kill him by wet or dry means, day or night, then broke it by killing him with sea foam. Namuchi's head pursued Indra, who went to Brahma. Brahma told him to bathe at the Aruna confluence with the Sarasvati and offer gifts, and Indra was freed.
shots.B09C043S02H01: Vaishampayana describes Balarama's bathing at the Soma tirtha, where Soma once performed the Rajasuya sacrifice, Atri was the priest, Skanda defeated Taraka, and Kartikeya is said to dwell under a great asvattha tree.

B09C044.summary: Janamejaya asks how Skanda was invested as commander of the celestial army. Vaishampayana tells how Shiva's seed fell into fire, passed to the Ganga and then to Himalaya, and grew into the child Skanda, who was nursed by the six Krittikas and grew six faces. The gods gathered to see him, Shiva divided himself into four forms to meet the four who were expecting him, and Brahma appointed Skanda commander. The gods then gathered by the Sarasvati at Himalaya.

scenes.B09C044S01: Janamejaya asks about Skanda's investiture, and Vaishampayana describes his birth, his nurture by the Krittikas, the gods' gathering, and his appointment as commander at the Sarasvati.

shots.B09C044S01H01: Janamejaya asks for the time, place, manner and officiants of Skanda's investiture and wants to know how he defeated the Daityas.
shots.B09C044S01H02: Vaishampayana tells how Shiva's seed fell into fire, then into the Ganga and onto Himalaya, where the child grew. The six Krittikas claimed him and he took six faces to nurse from each. The gods, Brahma and the others gathered, and Shiva divided himself into four forms to meet Skanda's choice. Brahma made Skanda commander of the celestial army, and the gods gathered at the Sarasvati's bank on Himalaya for the rites.

B09C045.summary: The gods and many other beings gather at Himalaya for Skanda's installation as commander. Brahma, Kasyapa and the others pour sacred water over him, and each god gives him companions and warriors. A long catalogue lists the many strange-looking followers who join him, and they dance in joy at his coronation.

scenes.B09C045S01: The gods and sages perform the installation rites for Skanda, each god gives him attendants, and a vast crowd of strange followers gathers around him.

shots.B09C045S01H01: Vaishampayana describes the rites of installation at Himalaya: Brihaspati makes the offerings, the gods and many others attend, Skanda is seated and anointed with water from the Sarasvati, and each god gives him companions. A long list follows of the many beings with odd faces and weapons who come to serve him, and they dance around him in joy.

B09C046.summary: Vaishampayana lists the mother goddesses who become Skanda's followers, describes their forms and powers, and lists the weapons and gifts the gods give him. Skanda sets out against the Daityas, kills Taraka and other demon chiefs, and pierces Mount Krauncha to destroy Vana. The chapter ends with Balarama bathing at Taijasa, the place where Varuna was installed.

scenes.B09C046S01: Vaishampayana introduces the mother goddesses who joined Kartikeya and begins to list their names.
scenes.B09C046S02: The list of mother goddesses continues.

scenes.B09C046S07: The list ends with a final group of names.
scenes.B09C046S08: The mothers are described, their forms and powers, and the gifts the gods give Skanda, including a dart, a banner and an army.
scenes.B09C046S09: Skanda sets out with his host and the gods' musicians, is granted a boon, and his army rushes at the Daityas, who flee.
scenes.B09C046S10: Skanda kills Taraka and other Daitya chiefs and pierces Mount Krauncha to slay Vana and the Daityas who fled there.
scenes.B09C046S11: Vaishampayana closes the account of Skanda's installation and tells how Balarama bathes at Taijasa, where Varuna was installed.

shots.B09C046S01H01: Vaishampayana introduces the large bands of mothers, the slayers of foes who became Kumara's companions.
shots.B09C046S01H02: He says he will name them, and that they pervade the mobile and immobile universe.
shots.B09C046S01H03: He asks Janamejaya to listen to the names of these illustrious mothers.
shots.B09C046S01H04: He says the mothers are auspicious and fill the whole universe.
shots.B09C046S01H05: The first names of the mothers are given, beginning with Prabhavati and Vishalakshi.
