shots.B09C046S07H05: The list closes with the last names, ending with Virocana.
shots.B09C046S08H01: The mothers, thousands in number, are described: long nails, large teeth, youthful and ornamented, able to change form, and of many complexions.
shots.B09C046S08H02: Their powers are described: they can grant boons, travel at will, and partake of the natures of many gods.
shots.B09C046S08H03: They are described as beautiful, strong and fearsome in battle, and as quick as the wind.
shots.B09C046S08H04: They live in trees, crossroads, caves, cremation grounds and mountains, and they speak many languages.
shots.B09C046S08H05: Indra gives Kartikeya a dart and a banner, Shiva gives him a great army, Vishnu a garland, Uma two cloths, and Ganga, Brihaspati, Garuda, Aruna, Varuna and Brahma other gifts, including victory in battle.
shots.B09C046S09H01: Skanda, now commander of the celestial forces, sets out with his companions and the mothers to destroy the Daityas, and his army is shown in splendour.
shots.B09C046S09H02: The gods' musicians play, and the gods praise Kartikeya while the Gandharvas sing and the Apsaras dance.
shots.B09C046S09H03: Skanda promises the gods that he will slay all who wish to slay them, and the gods regard their foes as already slain.
shots.B09C046S09H04: Skanda marches out with his army, and personified qualities such as success and courage lead the way.
shots.B09C046S09H05: The Daityas, Rakshasas and Danavas flee, and Skanda hurls his dart repeatedly, causing meteors and thunderbolts to fall, as at the end of the world.
shots.B09C046S10H01: Skanda kills Taraka with a hundred thousand Daityas around him, then kills Mahisha, Tripada and Hradodara with their followers.
shots.B09C046S10H02: Thousands of Daityas are burned by the dart, struck by banners, or fall at Skanda's roars. Skanda kills many foes.
shots.B09C046S10H03: Bali's son Vana attacks the gods from Mount Krauncha, and Skanda pierces the mountain with his dart, making the forests and creatures flee.
shots.B09C046S10H04: Skanda kills Bali's son and his brother, and the dart returns to his hand after each throw. The gods honour him.
shots.B09C046S10H05: The gods rejoice, and celestial women shower flowers. Different traditions name Skanda as a son of Sanat-kumara, Shiva, Agni, Uma, the Krittikas or Ganga.
shots.B09C046S11H01: Vaishampayana says the installation account is complete, that the tirtha became a second heaven, and that Balarama bathed at Taijasa, where Varuna was installed, and gave gifts.

B09C047.summary: Janamejaya asks how Varuna was installed as lord of the waters at this tirtha. Vaishampayana tells how the gods made Varuna lord of rivers and seas, and how Agni hid in a Sami tree after Bhrigu's curse until the gods found him. Balarama then visits Brahmayoni, the Kuvera tirtha and Vadarapachana.

scenes.B09C047S01: Janamejaya asks about Varuna's installation, Vaishampayana describes the gods' decision and Agni's hiding, and Balarama visits several holy places.

shots.B09C047S01H01: Janamejaya says the story is wonderful, that he feels purified, and asks how Varuna was installed as lord of the waters at this tirtha.
shots.B09C047S01H02: Vaishampayana tells how the gods asked Varuna to rule all rivers and seas, and how he accepted and was installed. Balarama bathes at Agnitirtha, where Agni had hidden in a Sami tree, and the gods went to Brahma when the fire disappeared.
shots.B09C047S01H03: Janamejaya asks why Agni, creator of the worlds, disappeared and how the gods found him.
shots.B09C047S01H04: Vaishampayana says Agni hid in the Sami tree after a curse from Bhrigu, and the gods searched and found him. Agni was made to eat everything, as Bhrigu said. Balarama then visits Brahmayoni, the Kauvera tirtha, where Kuvera gained his powers, and Vadarapachana, where fruits are always abundant.

B09C048.summary: At Vadarapachana, the maiden Sruvavati, daughter of Bharadwaja, does harsh penance to win Indra as her husband. Indra tests her by asking her to boil jujubes, and she burns her own feet to keep the fire going, and he grants her a boon. The place becomes a sacred tirtha, and Vaishampayana tells how Arundhati and Shiva first made it holy. Balarama then goes on to the tirtha of Sakta.

scenes.B09C048S01: Sruvavati's penance, her test by Indra in disguise, Indra's boon and the sanctity of Vadarapachana, the story of Sruvavati's birth, and Balarama's move on to Sakta.

shots.B09C048S01H01: Vaishampayana tells how Sruvavati, a Brahmacharini, does severe penance to win Indra. Indra, disguised as Vasishtha, asks her to boil jujubes, and she burns her feet to keep the fire going. Pleased, Indra reveals himself and grants her boon. The place becomes a holy tirtha named Vadarapachana, and the chapter recalls how Arundhati and Shiva made the place sacred in an earlier drought.
shots.B09C048S01H02: Janamejaya asks who Sruvavati's mother was and how she was raised.
shots.B09C048S01H03: Vaishampayana says Sruvavati was born when Bharadwaja's seed fell on seeing the Apsara Ghritachi, kept in a leaf cup. Bharadwaja named her and raised her, and Balarama bathes and gives gifts before going on to the tirtha of Sakta.

B09C049.summary: Balarama visits a string of sacred sites: Indra's tirtha, where Indra performed a hundred horse sacrifices; Rama's tirtha, where Parashurama gave the earth to his teacher; and the Yamuna, where Varuna performed a Rajasuya. He then reaches the Aditya tirtha, where Surya gained his power and where Vyasa and others live.

scenes.B09C049S01: Balarama bathes at Indra's tirtha, Rama's tirtha, the Yamuna and the Aditya tirtha, giving gifts at each, and names the sages who dwell at the last.

shots.B09C049S01H01: Vaishampayana describes Balarama's visits to Indra's tirtha, where Indra gained the name Satakratu after a hundred sacrifices, to Rama's tirtha, where Parashurama gave the earth to Kasyapa, to the Yamuna, where Varuna held a Rajasuya, and finally to the Aditya tirtha, where Surya gained his power. Vishnu bathed there, and Vyasa and Asita-Devala gained yogic powers there.

B09C050.summary: Vaishampayana tells the story of Asita-Devala, a householder of perfect equanimity, and his guest, the mendicant Jaigishavya. Devala finds Jaigishavya in two places at once, sees him travelling through the heavens, and is told he has gone to Brahman. Devala then renounces the householder's life for liberation under Jaigishavya's guidance. Narada criticises Jaigishavya, but the gods defend him, and Balarama bathes at this place before going on to the Soma tirtha.

scenes.B09C050S01: Devala's householder life and his guest Jaigishavya, Devala's flight through the heavens, the Siddhas' report, Devala's choice to follow the path of liberation, and Balarama's departure.

shots.B09C050S01H01: Vaishampayana introduces Asita-Devala, an impartial householder who gives hospitality, and his guest Jaigishavya, a yogi. Devala is puzzled when Jaigishavya seems to bathe in the ocean before him and then be found in his hermitage. Devala flies to the heavens and watches Jaigishavya pass through many worlds, then asks the Siddhas where he has gone.
shots.B09C050S01H02: The Siddhas tell Devala that Jaigishavya has gone to the eternal realm of Brahman.
shots.B09C050S01H03: Devala tries to follow, falls back, and the Siddhas tell him he cannot reach Brahman.
shots.B09C050S01H04: Devala returns to his hermitage, finds Jaigishavya there, and asks to take up the life of liberation. Jaigishavya teaches him. Creatures and plants lament the loss of a provider, but Devala chooses liberation and attains the highest success. Narada disparages Jaigishavya, and the gods praise him. Balarama bathes at this tirtha and goes on to Soma's tirtha.

B09C051.summary: Balarama visits the tirtha of the sage Sarasvata, who taught the Vedas during a twelve-year drought. Vaishampayana tells how Sarasvata was the son of the sage Dadhichi and the river Sarasvati, and how the gods later took Dadhichi's bones to make a thunderbolt for Indra. In the drought, Sarasvata fed the sages and then taught the Vedas to 60,000 of them. Balarama gives gifts and moves on.

scenes.B09C051S01: Balarama visits Sarasvata's tirtha, and Vaishampayana tells how Dadhichi's seed, held by the river Sarasvati, became her son Sarasvata.
scenes.B09C051S02: Indra needs Dadhichi's bones for a weapon, the sages are starving in the drought, and Sarasvata feeds and teaches them until they honour him as their teacher.

shots.B09C051S01H01: Vaishampayana says Balarama bathes at the place where the Lord of stars once performed the Rajasuya and a great battle with Taraka began, and then visits the tirtha of the sage Sarasvata, who taught the Vedas during a twelve-year drought.
shots.B09C051S01H02: Janamejaya asks why Sarasvata taught the Vedas during the drought.
shots.B09C051S01H03: Vaishampayana tells how the austere sage Dadhichi was tempted by Indra, who sent the Apsara Alambusa. Dadhichi's seed fell into the Sarasvati, which carried it until it became a child, Sarasvata.
shots.B09C051S01H04: The river gives the child to Dadhichi, saying she kept him through devotion, and Dadhichi blesses her waters for the gods and Apsaras.
shots.B09C051S01H05: Dadhichi praises the river and names the child Sarasvata. He says the boy will teach the Vedas in a drought and will make the river the foremost of holy rivers.
shots.B09C051S02H01: Indra, at war with the Danavas, finds no weapon able to kill them and is told that only Dadhichi's bones will do. He asks the gods to beg for them.
shots.B09C051S02H02: Dadhichi gives up his life, and Indra uses his bones to make thunderbolts and other weapons. Indra kills many Daityas, and a later twelve-year drought forces the sages to scatter.
shots.B09C051S02H03: The Sarasvati tells Sarasvata to stay, promising to supply him with large fish, and he feeds the sages and the gods.
shots.B09C051S02H04: After the drought, the sages have forgotten the Vedas, and they ask Sarasvata to teach them. He says ability matters more than age, and he teaches them.
shots.B09C051S02H05: Sixty thousand sages become his disciples and bring grass for his seat. Balarama gives gifts there and moves on to an old woman's asylum.

B09C052.summary: Janamejaya asks about a maiden who devoted herself to penance. Vaishampayana tells the story of the daughter of Kuni-Garga, who did penance without marrying until Narada said that she had no place in heaven without marriage. She offered half her merit to any husband, and the sage Sringavat accepted her for one night. She gave a boon to the tirtha and went to heaven, and Sringavat followed her. Balarama hears that Shalya has been killed and asks the sages about the battle.

scenes.B09C052S01: Janamejaya asks about the maiden, Vaishampayana describes her penance, Narada's words, and her offer of half her merit to a husband.
scenes.B09C052S02: The marriage of one night, the maiden's departure to heaven, Sringavat's death, and Balarama's news of the war.

shots.B09C052S01H01: Janamejaya asks why the maiden turned to penance, what her vow was, and asks for full details.
shots.B09C052S01H02: Vaishampayana describes Kuni-Garga, who created a daughter by his will and then died. She practised penance and worshipped the gods and ancestors for years, refusing marriage because she saw no suitable husband.
shots.B09C052S01H03: She continues her penance until she is too old to walk and resolves to depart for the other world.
shots.B09C052S01H04: Narada tells her she has no place in heaven because she did not marry, despite her great penance.
shots.B09C052S01H05: She offers half her penances to any sage who takes her hand, and Sringavat, son of Galava, accepts her on condition that she stays with him one night.
shots.B09C052S02H01: They marry according to rites, and she becomes a radiant young woman. Sringavat spends the night with her.
shots.B09C052S02H02: At morning she says the compact is fulfilled, promises a merit to those who spend a night at the tirtha, and departs for heaven.
shots.B09C052S02H03: Sringavat grieves for her and, accepting half her penances as agreed, follows her in death.
shots.B09C052S02H04: Balarama learns that Shalya has fallen, grieves for him, and asks the sages at Samantapanchaka for news of the battle, which they tell him in full.

B09C053.summary: The sages explain to Balarama that Samantapanchaka is the northern altar of Brahman and that Kurukshetra is named after King Kuru, who ploughed the field. Indra promised heaven to those who die there in battle or by fasting. The sages describe the sanctity of the land, its boundaries, and the blessings it brings.

scenes.B09C053S01: The sages tell Rama how Kuru ploughed the field and how Indra promised heaven to those who died there, and they describe its sanctity.

shots.B09C053S01H01: The sages say Samantapanchaka is Brahman's northern altar and that the field is called Kurukshetra after King Kuru, who cultivated it for many years.
shots.B09C053S01H02: Balarama asks why Kuru ploughed the field and asks the sages to explain.
shots.B09C053S01H03: The sages tell how Indra asked Kuru why he ploughed, and Kuru said those who die there will go to heaven. Indra mocked him, but the gods agreed to grant the promise. The sages describe the sanctity of the land, its benefits, its boundaries, and the verse that Indra sang in its praise.

B09C054.summary: Balarama visits a sacred hermitage, then climbs the Himalayan foothills through a series of tirthas. Narada arrives and tells him of the deaths of the Kuru heroes, the flight of the last three warriors, and Duryodhana's rise from the lake to face Bhima. Balarama sets out in his chariot to watch the duel between his two pupils.

scenes.B09C054S01: Balarama visits hermitages and tirthas, meets Narada, hears of the war and Duryodhana's challenge, and sets out for the field.

shots.B09C054S01H01: Balarama visits a hermitage linked to Vishnu and Sandilya's daughter, then proceeds up Himalaya through several tirthas. Narada arrives, and Balarama asks him for news of the battle and the field.
shots.B09C054S01H02: Narada reports the deaths of Bhishma, Drona, Jayadratha, Karna, Bhurishrava and Shalya, and says only Kripa, Kritavarma and Ashvatthama survive. Duryodhana, pierced by the Pandavas' words, has risen from the lake and is about to fight Bhima. Narada urges Balarama to hurry and watch the duel.
shots.B09C054S01H03: Balarama dismisses his companions to Dwaraka, praises the Sarasvati in a verse, and rides in his chariot to see the duel between his two pupils.

B09C055.summary: Dhritarashtra asks how his son fought Bhima once Balarama arrived. Sanjaya explains that Yudhishthira honoured Balarama, who praised Kurukshetra as a holy field where warriors who die go to heaven. Duryodhana and Bhima take their places on a sandless spot south of the Sarasvati, with their maces, and the kings and gods gather to watch them, as the two circle each other like great beasts.

scenes.B09C055S01: Dhritarashtra asks how the mace duel went, and Sanjaya describes Balarama's arrival, the honours shown to him, the preparations, and the two heroes facing each other while the crowd gathers to watch.

shots.B09C055S01H01: Vaishampayana introduces Dhritarashtra's grief as he asks about the duel.
shots.B09C055S01H02: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya how his son fought Bhima when Balarama came to watch.
shots.B09C055S01H03: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana's joy at Balarama's arrival and Yudhishthira's honours to him. Balarama praises Kurukshetra as a sacred field where warriors who die go to heaven, and the Pandavas and Duryodhana move to the chosen spot on the southern bank of the Sarasvati. Both champions, in armour and with maces, are compared to gods and great beasts. Duryodhana, sure of his strength, calls on the assembled kings to watch, and they sit down to see the combat.

B09C056.summary: Dhritarashtra laments that his son, once a lord of armies, must now fight on foot with a mace. Sanjaya describes frightful omens, and Bhima vows to avenge the Kauravas' wrongs and to kill Duryodhana. Duryodhana mocks Bhima's boasting and challenges him to act, and the crowd cheers them on as they advance.

scenes.B09C056S01: Dhritarashtra grieves over his son's humbling, Sanjaya describes the omens, and the two champions trade boasts and insults before they fight.

shots.B09C056S01H01: Dhritarashtra laments that his son, once lord of many armies and of the earth, now has to stand on foot with a mace, and says that this must be the work of fate.
shots.B09C056S01H02: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana's challenge, the omens of storm, thunder, eclipse and disturbed wells, and Bhima's long speech of vengeance listing the Kauravas' wrongs. Duryodhana answers with mockery that Bhima is a coward, and the kings cheer as the mace fighters advance.

B09C057.summary: The mace duel between Duryodhana and Bhima is long and even. The two strike and circle, and the gods and onlookers cannot tell who will win. Duryodhana strikes Bhima on the head and flank, and Bhima answers with a blow that drops Duryodhana to his knees. Duryodhana rises and knocks Bhima down, wrecking his chest armour. Bhima recovers and stands again, and the blows and circling continue until the end of the day.

scenes.B09C057S01: The mace duel between Duryodhana and Bhima rages, with each knocking the other down in turn, until Bhima gets up with his armour broken.

shots.B09C057S01H01: Sanjaya describes the duel in detail. The two circle, strike and retreat, until both are exhausted and rest. They resume, with the gods and onlookers astonished. Duryodhana wins the right side, Bhima the left, and Duryodhana strikes Bhima's flank. Bhima's mace fails to reach him, and Duryodhana strikes Bhima on the head. Bhima stands firm, Duryodhana is knocked down by Bhima's blow, Duryodhana rises and knocks Bhima down, and the Pandavas then cheer. Duryodhana strikes Bhima again, Bhima rises, and the fight goes on.
shots.B09C057S01H02: Sanjaya says Duryodhana's mace has broken Bhima's coat of mail and left him struck. Gods shower flowers, the Pandavas and their allies fear the outcome, and Bhima stands up again, with rolling eyes, steadying himself and preparing to fight on.

B09C058.summary: Arjuna asks Krishna who is the better fighter, and Krishna explains that Duryodhana has more skill but Bhima more strength. Krishna argues that Bhima must use a trick to win, and Arjuna gives Bhima a signal. Bhima strikes Duryodhana's thighs with his mace as Duryodhana jumps, breaking them, and Duryodhana falls with the sky and earth shaking around him.

scenes.B09C058S01: Arjuna asks Krishna to judge the two fighters, Krishna advises a trick, Arjuna gives Bhima the signal, and the duel ends with Duryodhana's thighs broken and portents filling the sky.

shots.B09C058S01H01: Arjuna asks Krishna which of the two fighters is better and what each one's merits are.
shots.B09C058S01H02: Krishna says the two were taught equally. Bhima is stronger, Duryodhana more skilled, and only deception will let Bhima win. He recalls Bhima's vow to break Duryodhana's thighs and blames Yudhishthira for staking the outcome on one duel. Arjuna slaps his thigh as a signal. Bhima and Duryodhana fight on until Bhima strikes Duryodhana's thighs with his mace as Duryodhana leaps. Duryodhana falls, and the sky, earth and creatures react with terrible omens.

B09C059.summary: Bhima stands over the fallen Duryodhana, mocks him for the old insults about Draupadi, and sets his foot on the king's head. The Somakas disapprove, and Yudhishthira rebukes Bhima for the insult and then mourns Duryodhana, blaming his fate and his own acts.

scenes.B09C059S01: Bhima taunts the fallen Duryodhana and places his foot on his head, Yudhishthira rebukes him, and Yudhishthira grieves for Duryodhana and the Kurus.

shots.B09C059S01H01: Sanjaya describes the Pandavas' joy and Bhima's taunts over the fallen Duryodhana, his foot on the king's head, and Yudhishthira's rebuke, which tells Bhima to stop crushing a king and kinsman, and then Yudhishthira's lament for Duryodhana and his own grief at the dead.

B09C060.summary: Dhritarashtra asks what Balarama did when Duryodhana was struck down. Sanjaya reports that Balarama condemned the blow below the navel and rushed at Bhima with his plough. Krishna stopped him by reminding him of the Pandava vow and Maitreya's curse, and Balarama left for Dwaraka. Krishna then asks Yudhishthira why he tolerated Bhima's act, and Yudhishthira explains his grief and his indifference. Bhima exults, and Yudhishthira tells his brothers the war is over.

scenes.B09C060S01: Dhritarashtra asks about Balarama's reaction, Balarama's rage and departure, and Krishna and Yudhishthira's exchange over Bhima's conduct.
scenes.B09C060S02: Bhima is praised by Krishna, claims the earth for Yudhishthira, and Yudhishthira declares the war is over.

shots.B09C060S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks what the mighty Balarama did when Duryodhana was struck down unfairly.
shots.B09C060S01H02: Sanjaya describes Balarama condemning Bhima's blow below the navel as contrary to the rules of the mace fight, raising his plough and rushing at Bhima. Krishna holds him back, citing Bhima's vow and Maitreya's curse, and Balarama argues about morality, profit and pleasure. Krishna says the Kali age is near and asks him to be calm.
shots.B09C060S01H03: Balarama, unconvinced, declares that Yudhishthira has slain Duryodhana unfairly and that Duryodhana died a fair warrior. He ascends his chariot and leaves for Dwaraka. Krishna then goes to Yudhishthira, who sits downcast and sorrowful.
shots.B09C060S01H04: Krishna asks Yudhishthira why he allows Bhima to place his foot on the head of the fallen Duryodhana.
shots.B09C060S01H05: Yudhishthira says he does not like the act, but he has looked on in grief at the Kauravas' cruel acts and their exile of the Pandavas. He lets Bhima do as he wishes.
shots.B09C060S02H01: Krishna accepts Yudhishthira's words, and Bhima, glad of his victory, salutes Yudhishthira and says the earth is his, with its enemies all dead.
shots.B09C060S02H02: Yudhishthira says the hostilities are over, that Duryodhana is struck down, that the earth is won by following Krishna's counsel, and that the debts to their mother and their anger are paid.

B09C061.summary: The Pandavas and Panchalas rejoice over Duryodhana's fall, and Krishna orders them to stop their taunts. Duryodhana, propped up and in agony, bitterly accuses Krishna of trickery and lists the Pandavas' tricks against the Kaurava warriors. Krishna answers with a list of Duryodhana's own crimes, and Duryodhana declares that he dies a fortunate king and will go to heaven while his enemies remain in misery.

scenes.B09C061S01: Dhritarashtra asks how the Pandavas reacted, the victors rejoice, Krishna rebukes them, Duryodhana and Krishna trade accusations, and Duryodhana declares his fortune.
scenes.B09C061S02: Flowers fall from heaven, and Krishna defends his deceptions as the only way to defeat warriors who could not be beaten fairly.

shots.B09C061S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what the Pandavas and Srinjayas did when Bhima struck down Duryodhana.
shots.B09C061S01H03: Sanjaya describes the Pandavas and Panchalas rejoicing and praising Bhima. Krishna tells them it is wrong to keep insulting a dead foe, since Duryodhana refused the Pandavas their share of the kingdom, and orders them to leave. Duryodhana, sitting up, glares at Krishna and begins to speak.
shots.B09C061S01H04: Krishna answers Duryodhana: he has been slain for his own sins, including refusing the Pandavas their share, poisoning Bhima, trying to burn them at the lacquer house, insulting Draupadi, cheating Yudhishthira at dice, and killing Abhimanyu. Duryodhana's own acts are the cause of his fall.
shots.B09C061S01H05: Duryodhana, in his last words, says he has studied, given gifts, ruled the earth and died in battle, a fortunate end for a Kshatriya. He will go to heaven with his brothers, while the Pandavas will be left in grief.
shots.B09C061S02H01: Flowers fall from heaven, the Gandharvas and Apsaras celebrate Duryodhana, and the Pandavas are ashamed. Krishna says the Kaurava warriors could not be beaten fairly, that he used illusion for their sake, and that when enemies are many, a foe must be defeated by any means, as the gods did.

B09C062.summary: The Pandavas go to Duryodhana's emptied tent, and Krishna has Arjuna get down first. Arjuna's chariot, already scorched by Drona and Karna, bursts into flames and is burnt to ashes after Krishna leaves it. Krishna then embraces Yudhishthira and praises the victory. The Pandavas take the Kaurava treasure, camp by the Oghavati, and send Krishna to Hastinapura to comfort Gandhari.

scenes.B09C062S01: The Pandavas enter the emptied Kaurava camp, and Arjuna's chariot burns to ashes when Krishna gets down from it.
scenes.B09C062S02: Krishna embraces Yudhishthira and praises the victory, and the Pandavas claim the Kaurava treasure.
scenes.B09C062S03: The Pandavas camp by the Oghavati, and Krishna sets out to comfort Gandhari in Hastinapura.

shots.B09C062S01H01: Sanjaya describes the Kaurava warriors going to their tents, the Pandavas and their allies going to Duryodhana's tent, and its empty, ruined state.
shots.B09C062S01H02: Krishna asks Arjuna to put down his bow Gandiva and the quivers and to dismount first, and says he will follow.
shots.B09C062S01H03: Arjuna dismounts, Krishna follows, and the celestial ape on the chariot flag vanishes. The chariot, already scorched in battle by Drona and Karna, bursts into flames and burns to ashes.
shots.B09C062S01H04: Arjuna asks Krishna why the chariot burned and asks him to explain.
shots.B09C062S01H05: Krishna explains that the chariot had been burnt by many weapons and only held together because he rode on it. Once Arjuna had won, Krishna left it, and it burned.
shots.B09C062S02H01: Krishna embraces Yudhishthira, praises the victory and the survival of the Pandavas, and urges him to act now.
shots.B09C062S02H02: Krishna recalls that at Upaplavya Yudhishthira asked him to protect Arjuna, and he agreed.
shots.B09C062S02H03: Krishna says he has kept Arjuna safe, and that Arjuna and the others have survived. Yudhishthira, with his hair standing on end, thanks him.
shots.B09C062S02H04: Yudhishthira praises Krishna's grace, which let him defeat Drona's and Karna's weapons, the Samsaptakas and the Kaurava armies, and notes Vyasa's words that victory follows Krishna.
shots.B09C062S02H05: The Pandavas enter Duryodhana's camp, take its treasure, jewels, cattle and slaves, and cheer their victory before resting their animals.
shots.B09C062S03H01: Krishna suggests that the Pandavas camp outside the main camp that night for an auspicious rite, and they camp at the banks of the Oghavati.
shots.B09C062S03H02: Krishna, with Daruka at the reins, sets out for Hastinapura, and the Pandavas ask him to comfort Gandhari, who has lost her sons.

B09C063.summary: Janamejaya asks why Krishna went again to Hastinapura after the war. Vaishampayana explains that Yudhishthira feared Gandhari's wrath over her sons' deaths and sent Krishna to calm her. Krishna speaks to Dhritarashtra about the causes of the war and to Gandhari about her own earlier words, comforts them both, and leaves in haste when he learns of Drona's son's plan to attack the Pandavas at night.

scenes.B09C063S01: Janamejaya asks about Krishna's mission, and Vaishampayana describes Yudhishthira's fear, Krishna's visit to Dhritarashtra and Gandhari, and his hurried departure to warn the Pandavas.

shots.B09C063S01H01: Janamejaya asks why Yudhishthira sent Krishna to Gandhari and why Krishna himself had to go, since the war was already won.
shots.B09C063S01H02: Vaishampayana says Yudhishthira feared Gandhari's wrath, and he sent Krishna to calm her. Krishna, arriving at Hastinapura, honours Vyasa, Dhritarashtra and Gandhari, and tells Dhritarashtra that the Pandavas were wronged, that the king's own folly caused the war, and that he must not blame them. He then comforts Gandhari, reminding her of her own earlier advice that victory follows righteousness. Krishna sees that Drona's son plans to kill the Pandavas by night, so he leaves quickly to protect them and returns to their camp to tell them what he has done.

B09C064.summary: Dhritarashtra asks what Duryodhana said as he lay broken on the field. Sanjaya reports Duryodhana's lament: he recalls his wealth, power and honour, accuses Bhima of an unfair blow, and sends messages to his parents and his allies. He calls on Ashvatthama to avenge him, and then sends the messengers away.

scenes.B09C064S01: Dhritarashtra asks about Duryodhana's last words, and Sanjaya reports Duryodhana's speech of pride, grief and farewell, including his message to the warriors.

shots.B09C064S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks what his son said after being kicked, with his thighs broken, lying on the ground in pride and anger.
shots.B09C064S01H02: Sanjaya describes Duryodhana, dusty and bleeding, gathering his hair and striking the ground, cursing Yudhishthira and Bhima for the unfair blow, and listing his past glories. He asks Sanjaya to tell his parents not to grieve and sends word to Ashvatthama, Kripa and Kritavarma. He then bids farewell to his friends and kinsmen and to the Kauravas who died before him, and asks Sanjaya to console his family. The messengers leave, weeping, and carry the news to Ashvatthama.

B09C065.summary: Ashvatthama, Kripa and Kritavarma, the last Kaurava warriors, find Duryodhana lying broken on the field. Ashvatthama laments his fate, and Duryodhana tells him that death is fated and that he dies in battle as a Kshatriya should. Ashvatthama swears to kill every Panchala that night, and Duryodhana has Kripa install him as commander. Ashvatthama embraces the king and leaves, and the king lies alone through the night. The chapter closes the Shalya Parva.

scenes.B09C065S01: Ashvatthama, Kripa and Kritavarma reach the dying Duryodhana, Ashvatthama vows vengeance, Duryodhana makes him commander, and the Shalya Parva ends.

shots.B09C065S01H01: Sanjaya describes the three surviving Kaurava warriors reaching the field where Duryodhana lies broken and bloodied, surrounded by carrion beasts. They dismount and sit around him. Ashvatthama laments his fall and recalls his past splendour. Duryodhana replies that death is fated and that he dies in battle as a Kshatriya should, rejoicing in his fortune. He tells them they have done their duty and that fate cannot be overturned. Ashvatthama swears to kill every Panchala that night, and Duryodhana has Kripa install him as commander. Ashvatthama embraces the king and leaves, and Duryodhana lies alone through the night, with the warriors pondering what to do next.
shots.B09C065S01H02: Closing line: the Shalya Parva ends.
shots.B09C065S01H03: Heading: the title of the Mahabharata.
shots.B09C065S01H04: Heading: the word 'of' within the title.
shots.B09C065S01H05: Heading: the attribution to Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa.
